analysis.title: Goldman Says Silver "Still Stuck" After Billions Of Spec-Selling, Puts Panic-Bid
key_insights: Silver is down roughly 3% in two weeks to $57.48 on Oct 22, 2026, and speculators are still selling. Goldman's Quinn titles his latest silver diary 'Silver Futures: Still Stuck'.

Managed Money sold $565mm of silver futures in the COT week to Oct 13, the 3rd straight week of selling for a cumulative $2.2bn. The mix was $160mm of long liquidation and $405mm of new shorts. December silver lost 3.4% over the period.
Managed Money net length is roughly $1.7bn, below the February trough and the lowest on Goldman's two-year chart (approximate, read off the chart). The same measure was above $9bn in summer 2025.
The dollar reached 1-year highs and gained 0.3% during the COT window, after a hot core CPI print raised rate-hike odds. Silver fell 6% in a day to a two-month low, about $56, on CPI day (Oct 14).

Over Oct 13-20 the dollar backtracked 0.5% and silver still fell another 2.6%. Zerohedge argues this breaks the second leg of Quinn's framework, because the dollar was previously seen as the only thing holding silver back.

Goldman's structural-demand baskets turned down. US Solar fell 4.7%, China Solar fell 1.6% and Data Centers fell 7.9% on memory, neocloud and credit-quality concerns. Data Centers and Solar stayed soft over the next five sessions.
Goldman's China Solar index has roughly halved from the high-60s in May to below 40 (approximate). It had tracked silver gross longs closely from May to July.

Quinn says part of the dollar stall came from AI unwinds, which also read negatively for silver. His companion note says Goldman's Hyperscaler basket lost 3.6% over Oct 13-16 as credit spread widening accelerated.

Silver futures aggregate open interest rose $1.6bn, mostly on the heaviest price-action day. Open interest rose from about 107k to about 114k contracts in mid-October as price fell, which the author reads as new shorts.
Normalized 25-delta put-call skew reached a 98% one-year rank. The 3-month skew moved from about -10 to near -3, the richest since the July spike (approximate).
Quinn sees an opportunity for a tactical bounce but says the Iran War and its dollar impact loom. Absent an end to the conflict, silver may struggle to rally unless FX energy betas dampen much more.

With Brent above $110, WTI near $99 and gold at $4,122, the gold/silver ratio is about 72, up from 70 two weeks earlier (author's calculation). Holders of August $90 silver digitals need a roughly 57% rally to pay out.

The author keeps a contrarian stance with a shorter fuse. The path is either a Hormuz de-escalation or an AI credit rout that turns Fed hiking talk into cutting talk. Late July's washed-out positioning was followed by a 15% rally in December silver over six weeks.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's US Solar basket fell 4.7% and China Solar fell 1.6%, and the baskets stayed soft over the next five sessions. They are used as barometers of silver's industrial demand.
Goldman's Data Center basket fell 7.9% on memory, neocloud and credit-quality concerns. The Hyperscaler basket lost 3.6% as credit spreads widened.

macro_indicators.reading: Reached 1-year highs and gained 0.3% over the COT window, then backtracked 0.5% over Oct 13-20
macro_indicators.interpretation: The dollar's retreat did not support silver, which suggests the dollar is not the only driver of the weakness.

macro_indicators.reading: Described as a hot print that lifted the dollar and raised rate-hike odds
macro_indicators.interpretation: Silver fell 6% in a day on the print. Traders added to bets on three more Fed hikes by end-2027.
Higher oil on Hormuz headlines lifts the dollar (the 'FX energy beta'), which pressures silver.
Reflects the same Iran-related energy bid.

macro_indicators.reading: Traders priced three more Fed rate hikes by end-2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: The author argues this pricing could reverse if the AI credit rout deepens.

trade_ideas.description: Contrarian long silver, with a shorter fuse than the Oct 9 call, as a crowded short setup squeezes (author's view, not a Goldman trade).
trade_ideas.rationale: Net length is at a two-year low, new shorts are piling in and skew is at a 98% one-year rank, which the author says tends to end in a violent squeeze.
trade_ideas.risk: Iran War and dollar strength via the FX energy beta, and a continued AI unwind.

risk_factors: Iran War escalation lifting Brent and the dollar.
Further AI and data-center credit unwinds hurting silver's industrial-demand story.
Hot inflation prints keeping Fed rate-hike pricing elevated.
Silver bounces may be short-lived unless FX energy betas dampen.
The author's contrarian squeeze call has not yet worked after two weeks.
charts_described: Goldman chart of Managed Money net positioning shows net length of roughly $1.7bn, below the February trough and the lowest on a two-year chart (approximate).
Goldman chart of Managed Money gross longs against an inverted dollar index shows them moving in lockstep, with gross longs at roughly half the May peak as the dollar index pushed toward 102.5.
Goldman's China Solar index has roughly halved from the high-60s in May to below 40 (approximate, read off the chart).
Aggregate silver futures open interest chart shows a rise from about 107k to about 114k contracts in mid-October as price fell to the $56 area.
Normalized 3-month 25-delta put-call skew chart shows a move from about -10 to near -3, the richest since the July spike (approximate).
vol_and_positioning: Managed Money net length in silver is roughly $1.7bn, the lowest on Goldman's two-year chart (approximate), versus above $9bn in summer 2025.
Managed Money gross longs have slid to roughly $4.7bn, about half the roughly $9.3bn May peak, and track an inverted dollar index (approximate, garbled in source).
Silver futures aggregate open interest rose $1.6bn, from about 107k to about 114k contracts, with price falling to the $56 area.
Normalized 25-delta put-call skew hit a 98% one-year rank. The 3-month skew moved from about -10 to near -3, the richest since the July spike (approximate).
Positioning is described as washed out. After late July's similar reading, December silver rose 15% in six weeks.
geopolitical: The Iran War and escalating Iranian attacks on shipping around Hormuz are keeping Brent and the dollar bid.
Zerohedge says the attacks are escalating into the US midterms.
A Hormuz de-escalation is named as one possible trigger for a silver rally.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's FX team's call that dollar upside 'could stall' has so far worked for about five sessions.

tension_points.bull_case: Net length is at a two-year low, new shorts are piling in and skew is at a 98% one-year rank. The author says this setup tends to end in a violent squeeze, as in late July when December silver rose 15% in six weeks.
tension_points.bear_case: Quinn says the Iran War and its dollar impact loom, and silver may struggle to rally unless FX energy betas dampen. The AI and solar demand baskets are also falling.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An absence of a Hormuz de-escalation or a deeper AI credit rout turning Fed hiking talk to cutting talk would leave silver stuck. Zerohedge will check after Friday's COT whether the $1.6bn of new open interest was shorts.
